Kayla: Hey team — quick compliance question about onboarding Copperhead-7b (we tested PTQ 4-bit). The upstream repo has a weird clause, can we: 1) host a quantized variant behind our API, 2) ship a container with qweights to a partner, and 3) display an attribution banner in-app to satisfy the license?

Dennis: From infra side, hosting the quantized model behind API should be trivial. We already benchmarked it: 220ms p99 on p4d for 512 tokens. But shipping qweights tarballs is the risky one. :grimacing:

Clare: can you paste the exact license snippet? I skimmed earlier but didn't memorize.

Kayla: sure — here's the short block from LICENSE.md from the upstream:```
Redistribution of model weights (original or modified) is prohibited except for academic or internal research. Serving models via an API endpoint is permitted provided attribution is displayed and the provider does not redistribute the raw weight files.```

legal-bot: automated-note: link to source repo LICENSE: https://git.example.com/copperhead/COPYING (found by license-scan).

Clare: thanks. High-level: serving behind an API is allowed per that text, as long as you also provide attribution. Shipping the quantized weight files to partners looks like redistribution and would be disallowed without a separate commercial license.

Dennis: clarifying question — does quantization count as "modified" weights (so redistribution of qweights would be banned)? Or is PTQ considered a runtime transform?

Clare: good question. The clause says "original or modified" which is broad. Our interpretation: transforming weights (quantizing) produces a derivative artifact — still a form of redistribution if you ship it. So sending qweights tarball = redistribute "modified" weights, blocked by default.

Ryan: If we wrap the model in a container and give partner access to run the container on their infra (they get the image with weights inside), that's functionally the same as redistribution, right?

Clare: yes. Providing an image that contains the weights is effectively redistribution. The only safe shipping option under current license is source code or configs that don't include the weights.

Kayla: ok — so allowed: host behind API + show attribution. Not allowed: ship qweights or container with weights. Good to know. Two follow-ups: 1) is an attribution banner copy-paste enough or do they require specific wording/placement? 2) can we expose embeddings produced by the model to customers (they'll store vectors downstream)?

Clare: attribution: the clause doesn't specify format, but best practice is: short visible statement in-app and in API docs + include a reference in billing/terms where applicable. Something like "Models served by Redwood Inference: Copperhead-7b (upstream repo)" and a link to the repo should be fine. Capture this in the onboarding checklist.

Clare: embeddings: license doesn't usually restrict outputs (text/embeddings) unless there's an explicit "output restriction" clause. I didn't see one in this license, so embedding outputs are ok to return and customers can store them. But add a note: if the model training data includes copyrighted datasets with special output limits, that could change things — flag for legal review if the model metadata indicates such restrictions.

Dennis: noted. We did find a dataset provenance file mentioning a closed scraped dataset; I'm going to attach that to the model ticket for legal to review.

Kayla: thanks. For the partner who asked for an on-prem beta, suggested path is partner signs a commercial redistribution addendum?

Clare: yes — you can request a separate commercial redistribution license from the upstream authors. In the meantime, offer them a dedicated-hosting deployment (we host in their VPC or Dedicated) where we expose the inference API but do not hand over weights. That often satisfies enterprise needs and avoids license violation.

Ryan: operational note: for dedicated hosting we need to document the attribution and include a clause in the partner contract that they won't extract weights. I'll open infra ticket to add telemetry that detects weight export attempts (hash checks).

Kayla: perfect. I'll update the model-onboarding card with: "API-only serving allowed; qweights/container distribution prohibited without addendum; attribution required; embeddings allowed; escalate dataset provenance to legal."

Clare: thanks — I'll draft a short standard attribution blurb we can paste into Console and docs.

Dennis: small ops question — does the license permit us to ship performance numbers (benchmarks) publicly? e.g., "Copperhead-7b: 220ms p99 on p4d"

Clare: publishing benchmarks is generally ok; it's not redistributing weights. Avoid including snippets of the model code or weight extracts. If the upstream license had a privacy clause about training data provenance, double-check before publishing anything that references datasets.

Kayla: OK great. Action items: Kayla — update onboarding ticket; Dennis — attach dataset provenance; Ryan — infra ticket for export detection; Clare — attribution blurb + confirm dataset review window. Thanks all :thumbsup:

legal-bot: automated-note: tag created: compliance-required, owner=Clare, due=+5d.

Kayla: thanks! I'll move this to the onboarding board and mark blocked until legal confirms dataset provenance. :white_check_mark:
